messages:
IncidentBot: Paging: SEV2 - dedicated pool for Orca Therapeutics (orca-tenant) showing elevated 5xx and latency spikes on canary traffic. Alert: orca-dedicated-pool::canary-errors > 5% for 3m. @oncall-escalation sent.

Jordan (oncall): got it, I'm on. quick snapshot: errors are mostly model inference failures (invalid tokenization) + 2x latency for sequences >512. Canary started 12:14 UTC, spike at 12:27.

Carla (SE): Orca reported degraded responses in their staging traffic. They see truncated outputs and "token mismatch" messages in client logs. Impact: only canary subset (~3% of traffic) on dedicated pool, but they want immediate rollback if it affects production.

Ben (SRE): looking at runtime logs now. stacktraces point to artifact model-ggml-ort:v2.1-pin failing when sequence length >512 due to tokenizer change. Repro on a node: see snippet: 
```
ERR inference: tokenizer::decode: unknown token id 50256
WARN kvcache: invalidation mismatch
```

Ben (SRE): hypothesis: pinned artifact introduced an incompatible tokenizer build. Traffic fallback should go to pinned fallback version v2.0-stable. Recommend pinback to previous artifact and divert canary immediately.

Tom (ops): ready to execute. Plan: 1) divert canary routing to fallback pool 2) pin canary instances to model-ggml-ort:v2.0-stable 3) restart canary workers 4) verify.

Jordan (oncall): @DeployBot can you create a redeploy job and pin? Also tagging @Carla for customer comms.

DeployBot: Deploy job created: redeploy/orca-canary/pinback-2200001234. Running job. CI: passed for v2.0-stable image.

Tom (ops): running commands now: 
```
# divert canary traffic away from canary nodes
routectl set traffic --tenant orca --subset canary --weight 0 --to fallback
# pin artifact on canary deployment
kubectl -n orca set image deploy/orca-canary model=registry.redwood/model-ggml-ort:v2.0-stable
kubectl -n orca rollout restart deploy/orca-canary
```

Tom (ops): kubectl rollout started, pods coming up. first new pod ready at +40s.

Ben (SRE): watching metrics: canary error rate dropping from 7.3% -> 0.8% in last 2m after divert. Latency back to baseline ~120ms. Good sign.

Carla (SE): I told Orca support contact: "we've temporarily diverted canary traffic and pinned your canary to the previous stable artifact. No changes to your production pool. We'll confirm full verification before re-enabling canary." Customer acknowledged. :white_check_mark:

Diane (sec): any data exfil/exposure concerns? the error is tokenizer mismatch only, no PII leakage observed in logs. marking for audit but low risk.

Jordan (oncall): fine-grain verification: running sample payloads for long sequences. Repro test: 10k tokens through v2.0-stable passes. 

Sara (PM): what's the rollback ETA? Orca wants ETA to re-enable canary.

Ben (SRE): ETA to re-enable: after 30m of stable metrics and a quick canary smoke in staging. Recommend hold until we reproduce tokenizer change in a safe environment and coordinate a safe model upgrade path.

Tom (ops): I've pinned the artifact in the deploy config and pushed a policy to prevent auto-upgrades for orca canary. Config diff: 
```
- model_artifact: registry.redwood/model-ggml-ort:latest
+ model_artifact: registry.redwood/model-ggml-ort:v2.0-stable # pinned at 2200001234
auto_update: false
```

Jordan (oncall): starting on-call handoff in 15m. Tom will take over post-rollback monitoring. @Oncall-Handoff-Bot please record.

Oncall-Handoff-Bot: Handoff event recorded: from Jordan -> Tom. Start: 12:44 UTC. Escalation policy unchanged.

Tom (ops): taking over monitoring. Will keep canary diverted until midnight UTC or until we get approval from Product/SE.

Carla (SE): Customer follow-up: we'll schedule a joint test with Orca tomorrow to validate tokenizer compatibility with any new model builds. Also recommending we run full tokenization regression suite in CI for model artifact uploads.

Ben (SRE): opened a ticket to block artifact publish that changes tokenizer ABI without bumping compatibility flag: RN-4356. Also capturing regen steps to reproduce locally.

Jordan (oncall): adding postmortem notes to incident: include timeline, root cause (tokenizer ABI change in v2.1-pin), mitigation (divert + pinback), and follow-ups (CI regression, artifact publishing policy).

DeployBot: Job redeploy/orca-canary/pinback-2200001234 completed successfully. All canary pods on v2.0-stable.

Ben (SRE): final check: error rate steady at 0.5% for 10m, latency stable. Marking as mitigated. Recommendation: keep canary disabled until compatibility tests are green.

Carla (SE): I'll send a short customer update: "We've mitigated anomalous canary behavior by pinning your canary to last known-good artifact and diverting traffic. No production impact. We'll coordinate a safe upgrade window."

Sara (PM): thanks team. Please capture runbook tweaks for dedicated pool artifact pinning and add a safety gate for tokenizer-breaking changes.

Jordan (oncall): closing immediate paging. Handing off monitoring to Tom for the next 4 hours. If any regression, re-paging SRE. Great work. :clap:

Oncall-Handoff-Bot: Handoff complete. New oncall: Tom (ops).

Tom (ops): note for postmortem: we should add an alert for sudden tokenizer error spikes and a runbook step to check artifact compatibility matrix before canary promotion.

IncidentBot: Incident marked MITIGATED. Severity downgraded to SEV3. Postmortem assigned to: Ben (SRE), Carla (SE). Due: 72h.

Jordan (oncall): thanks all. closing thread once postmortem ticket is filed.

Carla (SE): filing follow-up with Orca and scheduling joint validation slot.

Ben (SRE): created postmortem RN-7890; linking to this thread and logs: https://internal.redwood/logs/2200001234

Tom (ops): leaving final note: rollback performed at 12:34 UTC, divert completed at 12:35 UTC, monitoring until 16:45 UTC.

Diane (sec): adding this incident to compliance log (no data exposure).

Jordan (oncall): thread closed. Good job everyone.
